frequency_question: How often do central banks deploy an incremental reserve ratio requirement within a specified window when banking system liquidity reaches structural surplus states?
membership_rule: Includes any formal central bank policy action mandating an incremental or marginal reserve requirement on deposit liabilities to absorb surplus liquidity. Excludes standard permanent changes to baseline reserve requirements.

cases.name: PBoC RRR hikes during 2010-2011 liquidity surges
RBI incremental CRR 2006 (outside strict window but analogous)

provenance_note: claimed 1 hits but 3 of 3 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases; rate of 100% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 major episodes identified for the specific central bank; sample is small because extraordinary iCRR tools are rarely used outside of extreme liquidity surplus events.
known_gaps: Excludes minor fine-tuning operations like variable rate reverse repos (VRRR) which are routine rather than incremental reserve ratios.
skeleton: RBI liquidity management episodes since 2010 characterized by large overhangs of surplus funds due to external factors (e.g., currency intervention or government spending surges): roughly 2 major liquidity overhang episodes requiring extraordinary absorption tools in 15 years.
multiplier: 2 episodes total across 15 years, with 1 resulting in an iCRR deployment.
validity_reason: Central bank operating frameworks and liquidity management toolkits evolve slowly over multi-year horizons.
